# How Can I Automate Communication Between Cleaning and Reception?


You automate the handoff by letting the "cleaned and ready" status update automatically the moment cleaning completes, releasing the property for the next check-in without a manual call or message. On **Jestor** , this connects cleaning task status directly to the property record.


The transition between cleaning and reception is a classic short stay delay point, cleaning finishes, but no one tells reception until someone remembers to check manually.


## What manual handoff communication costs


- The cleaning team finishing, but reception not knowing until they check manually
- A delay between actual cleaning completion and the property being released for check-in
- No clear record of exactly when cleaning was completed
- Inconsistent communication depending on who is on shift for each team


## How automated cleaning-to-reception handoff works


- Completing a cleaning task can automatically trigger a property status change
- That status change automatically releases the property for the next check-in
- Reception sees the updated status in real time, no need to ask
- **SLA** shows how long cleaning is taking, giving both teams visibility


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Event-triggered automation removes the need for manual communication between teams
- Both teams work from the same property record, not separate systems
- SLA tracking makes visible whether the transition is taking longer than expected
- Reduces idle time between checkout, cleaning, and the next check-in


Manual communication Automated communication


Reception waits to be told manually Status updates automatically on completion


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does this work with outsourced cleaning teams?** Yes, as long as they log task completion in the same system. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Does reception need to check manually?** No, the status updates automatically and stays visible in real time.


**Does this apply to multiple properties at once?** Yes, the same automation applies to any connected property.
